message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: "!contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip release]')"

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build plugin
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify build artifacts
        run: |
          ls -la main.js styles.css manifest.json
          echo "Build artifacts verified"

      - name: Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: npx semantic-release",
  "rationale": "The release job has no explicit timeout, so a stuck or runaway run can consume the full default runner allowance. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is evidence-supported, reporting reduced runaway consumption (free 12.9%, paid 8.1% VM-time reduction), and the matching experiment example shows adding timeout-minutes to a job preserved all checks while bounding elapsed time. The workflow already caches npm dependencies via setup-node (cache: 'npm'), so a separate dependency cache would be redundant/contraindicated, and this is a single-job release workflow so matrix fail-fast, stale-run cancellation, and path filtering do not apply. Adding a generous 30-minute timeout bounds runaway consumption with operational headroom for npm ci, the tailwind/tsc/esbuild build, and semantic-release, without removing any step, changing permissions, adding secrets, or introducing new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
